Facts: Sun (defendant) drunk, angry, broke into Zhang's house (trespassing? but main act: vandalism, property damage). He entered by climbing over wall (illegal entry) and destroyed TV, audio, clothes, some burned. Value 1580 yuan. Then later he threatened via message to jump into house? Actually "要跳到其家中" maybe means "to jump into his house"? He threatened, causing fear. Zhang called his brother-in-law, police called. After, they reached compensation agreement, victim forgave.

So crimes: Intentional destruction of property (故意毁坏财物). Also possibly illegal entry (非法侵入住宅) but Chinese criminal law includes "非法侵入住宅罪" (trespassing). However typical charges in examples: For property damage they used "故意毁坏财物". Example: earlier case with assault and property damage: they used "故意毁坏财物". For violent assault they used "故意伤害". Here there is also assault: Zhang used fist to hit Sun? Actually "张某某回家制止被被告人孙某某用拳打到脸部." Wait reading: "张某某回家制止被被告人孙某某用拳打到脸部." Means Zhang returned home to stop Sun, and Sun punched Zhang in the face? Actually grammar: "张某某回家制止被被告人孙某某用拳打到脸部。" Could be: Zhang returned home to stop Sun, and Sun punched Zhang in the face. So Sun also inflicted bodily injury (punch to face). The victim's injury? Not described severity, but likely minor. Could be "故意伤害". However the description: "张某某回家制止被被告人孙某某用拳打到脸部。" Means Zhang was punched in the face by Sun. That is an assault causing injury. So Sun committed assault (故意伤害). The injury severity not given; maybe minor, but still a crime.

Thus charges: 故意毁坏财物; 故意伤害.

Check examples: For similar case where both property damage and assault, they used "故意伤害;故意毁坏财物". Example: earlier with Song case: they had both "故意伤害;故意毁坏财物". So order maybe "故意伤害;故意毁坏财物". In that example, they had assault causing heavy injury and property damage. So we can list both.

Any other charge? Threat via message could be "敲诈勒索"? Not exactly, just threat. Not enough.

Thus final answer: [罪名]故意伤害;故意毁坏财物<eoa>
